{"title":"The Dino Team by the Sea","level":2,"topic":"dinosaurs","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya reads about dinosaurs each day. She sees a team of them by the sea.

A big dino eats leaves. He is tall. He can reach the green leaves on a tall tree. Munch, munch!

A small dino eats meat. She is fast. She runs on the sand near the sea.

One dino has a long neck like a boat mast. He goes down to drink. He can float! His neck stays up.

Rain starts to fall. Drip, drip on the leaves. The dinos do not mind the rain. They play in the mud and wait.

Soon the rain goes away. The sun is out. A dino lets out a loud roar. Beat, beat go his big feet on the trail.

Maya reads the last page. Dinosaurs are real, and she can learn more each day. She will read again soon!","cover_scene":"A long-necked dinosaur wading in shallow sea water while a small fast dinosaur runs on the sandy beach under a rainbow."}

{"title":"Dino Eggs in the Oak Tree Trail","level":2,"topic":"dinosaur eggs","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya and Jean hike on the oak trail. They seek dinosaur eggs.

"Wait!" says Jean. "I see a nest!"

Three eggs sit on a heap of leaves. Each egg is real. Each egg is the size of a loaf of bread!

A mail truck goes past. The man waves. Maya waves back.

Then they hear a peep. Peep, peep! One egg cracks. A tiny dino peeks out. His neck is neat and long. His feet are teal green!

The baby dino eats a leaf. Then he eats three more leaves. He needs to eat a lot to grow tall.

Maya reads that big dinos once laid eggs like this. Real scientists dig them up today!

The baby dino sleeps by the oak. Maya and Jean tiptoe away. They wave and say, "Sleep well, little dino!"","cover_scene":"A nest of three big eggs under a tall oak tree with one egg cracking open and a tiny green dinosaur peeking out."}

{"title":"Ten Dino Eggs Roll Down the Road","level":2,"topic":"dinosaur eggs","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Ten dino eggs roll down the road. Maya sees them all!

The first egg cracks. Out leaps a T. rex. He lets out a great big roar!

The next egg cracks. Out peeks a Stegosaurus. His plates gleam in the sun.

Egg three has a Triceratops. She eats green leaves off a tree. Munch!

Egg four holds a small raptor. He speeds down the road on quick feet.

Egg five is soaked by rain. Out floats a long-neck dino. He reaches way up high.

More eggs crack. Six, seven, eight, nine, ten! Each one is a treat to meet.

The dinos need a home. Maya leads the team to a coast with soft sand and tall trees.

"Stay here," she says. "Eat and sleep and play."

Ten dinos cheer. Maya beams. What a day!","cover_scene":"Ten colorful dinosaur eggs rolling down a curving road, a few cracking open with baby dinosaurs peeking out, as a girl watches with delight."}

{"title":"The Dino Boat Race","level":2,"topic":"dinosaur boats","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya paints a big boat. Her dino pals want to race on the lake.

T. rex hops in a red boat. Its sail is real cloth. It flaps in the wind.

Stegosaurus takes a green boat. He floats fast! His tail helps him steer.

Triceratops picks a teal boat with a long oar. She rows and rows.

"Ready, set, go!" Maya yells.

The boats speed down the lake. Rain starts to fall. Drip, drip! No one quits.

T. rex leads. Then a gust fills the green sail. Stegosaurus goes past him!

Triceratops keeps her pace. She does not moan. She just rows.

At the last bend, all three boats meet. They reach the coast at the same beat!

"A tie!" Maya cheers. Each dino gets a treat: a heap of sweet green leaves.

What a great day to sail.","cover_scene":"Three cartoon dinosaurs in small colorful sailboats racing across a lake in light rain, with a girl cheering from a dock."}
Noted.

Dinosaur Patrol presents a thrilling maritime world waiting for your daring rescue missions! Dive into a world teeming with mysterious sea creatures and ancient dinosaurs."

{"title":"Dino Patrol on the Deep Sea","level":2,"topic":"dino rescue","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Beep! Beep! The alarm goes off.

"Dino Patrol!" yells Maya. "We need to sail!"

Maya and her dino team leap into the patrol boat. The boat floats out on the deep sea.

"Who needs aid?" asks Maya.

She sees a sea beast stuck in a heap of weeds. It lets out a sad moan.

T. rex leans out. He cuts the weeds with a neat snap.

The beast is free! It leaps and makes a big splash. Maya gets soaked by the rain of waves. She just laughs.

Then the beast leads the boat to a cave. Inside is a real dino egg!

The team keeps the egg warm on a coat.

Crack! A tiny dino peeks out. He eats a green leaf and squeaks.

"Great job, team," says Maya. "Dino Patrol saves the day!"","cover_scene":"A bright rescue patrol boat on a deep blue sea with a small girl and cartoon dinosaurs aboard, freeing a friendly sea creature tangled in seaweed."}

{"title":"Dino and the Snow Day","level":2,"topic":"dino friends","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Snow falls on the hill. Dino wakes up and cheers!

"Let's go play!" he calls to his friends.

Maya pulls her sled up the trail. Dino runs behind her. His big feet go crunch, crunch in the snow.

They zoom down the hill. Whee!

At the foot of the hill, they hear a squeak. A baby goat is stuck in deep snow!

"We can help," says Maya.

Dino digs with his tail. Maya reaches in. Up comes the goat! He is cold but safe.

Maya wraps him in her coat. Dino breathes warm air on him. Soon the goat feels fine.

The goat leaps and bleats. He wants to play too!

They all ride the sled down the hill again. Snow flies like sea foam.

"Best snow day ever," says Maya. Dino gives a happy roar.","cover_scene":"A friendly green dinosaur and a girl on a red sled zooming down a snowy hill with a small white goat riding along."}

{"title":"Dino and Friends Bake a Cake","level":2,"topic":"dino baking","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"T. rex has a plan. "Let's bake a cake for Dino!" he says. "It is his birthday."

Maya reads the recipe out loud.

"We need oats," she says. T. rex pours in the oats.

"We need cream." Maya beats the cream till it is light as foam.

"We need three eggs." Crack, crack, crack!

They mix and mix. Then they heat the oven and wait.

Soon a sweet smell floats in the air. The cake is done!

Maya spreads pink cream on top. T. rex adds green leaves made of jam.

Then they hear big feet on the road. Dino is home!

"Surprise!" they all yell.

Dino beams. He takes a deep breath and blows out each candle.

They each eat a slice. The cake is a real treat.

"Best day ever," says Dino.","cover_scene":"A group of cheerful cartoon dinosaurs and a girl around a kitchen table with a big frosted birthday cake topped with candles."}

Let's make a colourful cake and learn all the colours with our prehistoric friend. Dino is a small dinosaur with a big appetite for learning ..."

{"title":"Dino Paints the Cave","level":2,"topic":"dino colors","target_skill":"silent_e","text":"Dino has a cave. The cave is plain and gray.

"I will make it bright!" says Dino.

Maya brings paint. They take five cans up the slope.

Dino dips his tail in the red can. He makes a wide stripe on the stone wall.

Maya paints a blue lake with one white whale.

T. rex paints a green vine. He paints a pale pink rose, too.

They paint a big sun. They paint a home. They paint a plate of cake!

By nine, the cave is not plain. It is like a huge rainbow.

Dino smiles a wide smile. "This is the same cave, but it feels brand-new!"

Maya wipes her hands. "Can we paint mine next time?"

"Yes!" says Dino. "Name the shade and I will bring it."","cover_scene":"A small dinosaur dipping its tail in paint to make colorful stripes on a cave wall while a girl paints a blue lake beside him."}

{"title":"Dino and the Rainbow Kite","level":2,"topic":"dino kite","target_skill":"silent_e","text":"It is a fine, windy day. Dino has a kite.

The kite has nine stripes. Red, lime green, pale blue, and more. It is like a rainbow on a rope.

Maya takes the line. Dino gives a shove. Up, up goes the kite!

It sails above the pine trees. It dives and rises again.

Then a gust yanks the line. The kite slips away and lands on a huge stone spike!

"Oh no," says Maya. "It is stuck."

Dino makes a plan. He stands close and stretches his long spine. He is quite tall!

With his nose, he nudges the kite. It comes free!

Maya smiles a wide smile. "You save the day!"

They race home before five. The rainbow kite waves like a flame in the sky.","cover_scene":"A dinosaur and a girl flying a bright rainbow-striped kite above tall pine trees on a windy day."}

{"title":"The Dino-Powered Kite Test","level":2,"topic":"kite test","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya reads about a dino kite that really takes flight. She wants to make one too.

"We need a plan," she says to her team.

T. rex tapes a long tail on the kite. Dino paints green leaves on it.

They take the kite to the beach. The sea air feels cool.

Maya runs on the sand. The kite lifts, then drops with a thud.

"Try again," says Dino.

They wait for a breeze. Maya runs. The kite lifts, then falls in a heap.

"One more try," Maya says. "This time, Dino can help."

Dino takes a deep breath. He blows! Whoosh! The air sweeps under the kite.

Up it goes! It floats high above the waves. It soars past each cloud.

The team cheers. Dino-power works!","cover_scene":"A dinosaur blowing a big puff of air to lift a green leaf-painted kite high above a sunny beach as a girl runs holding the string."}

{"title":"Maya Meets the Octopus","level":2,"topic":"aquarium octopus","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya goes to the aquarium with Dino.

First they see a big gray seal. He floats on his back and claps.

Then they see a school of fish. The fish gleam like coins in the deep blue water.

"Look!" says Maya. "An octopus!"

The octopus has eight long arms. Each arm has neat rows of dots. He can squeeze into a tiny gap in the rocks.

Dino leans close to the glass. The octopus reaches out one arm. It looks like he waves hello!

"He can change his shade," reads Maya. "Red, then teal, then pale."

The octopus sails away and eats a treat.

On the way home, Dino asks, "Did dinos meet sea beasts too?"

"Yes," says Maya. "Long ago, huge beasts swam in the seas."","cover_scene":"A girl and a small dinosaur pressed against an aquarium window as a bright orange octopus stretches one arm toward them."}

{"title":"Eight Arms Help Out","level":2,"topic":"octopus helper","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Deep in the warm sea, an octopus wakes up. His eight arms stretch out wide.

He has round eyes and no bones at all. He can fit in a small crack in the reef!

Today he wants to help his pals.

A crab is stuck in a coil of rope. The octopus reaches down. One arm loops and pulls. The crab is free!

A baby eel needs a home. The octopus scoops sand and stacks neat stones. Now the eel has a safe cave.

Then a big shark speeds by. The octopus turns pale gray, just like the stones. The shark sails past and sees no one!

At last he floats home to his den. He eats a treat and sleeps.

Eight arms make a great team.","cover_scene":"A smiling orange octopus on a coral reef using its eight arms to free a small crab from a tangled rope."}

{"title":"Three Hearts in the Shallow Sea","level":2,"topic":"octopus facts","target_skill":"digraphs","text":"Maya and Dino splash in the shallow sea. They wish to find the octopus.

"Shh," says Maya. "Look! He is such a champ at hiding."

The octopus shifts his shade. He looks like a shell. Then he looks like a chunk of rock!

Dino chats with him. "Is it true you have three hearts?"

"Yes!" says the octopus. "Thump, thump, thump. Three hearts push my blue blood."

"Wow," whispers Maya.

A shark swims by. The octopus shoots a dash of ink. Whoosh! The shark cannot see. He rushes off.

Then the octopus shows them his shelf of shells. He shares a starfish with Dino.

The sun sinks. Maya must go.

"Thanks for the fun!" she shouts.

Eight arms wave. Three hearts thump. What a chum!","cover_scene":"An octopus hiding among colorful shells in shallow sunlit water while a girl and a small dinosaur peek at it from above the surface."}

{"title":"Dino's Deep Sea Ship","level":2,"topic":"sea adventure","target_skill":"digraphs","text":"Dino builds a ship. It is thick and strong.

"Let's check the deep sea!" he shouts.

Maya hops in. The ship chugs out past the wharf.

Splash! Down they go. Fish flash by the glass.

"Which way?" asks Dino.

"That way," says Maya. "To the shipwreck!"

The shipwreck rests in the sand. Shells cling to it. A crab pinches at a chain.

Then a shape shifts in the shade. It is the octopus!

He has no shell and no bones. He can slip in a thin crack much smaller than his head.

"Wow!" whispers Dino.

The octopus shows them a chest. Inside are shiny dishes and a gold chunk.

"We should leave it," says Maya. "This is his shop, not ours."

The octopus waves. The ship rushes up. What a champ of a trip!","cover_scene":"A small submarine-like ship beside a sunken shipwreck deep underwater with an octopus opening an old treasure chest."}

{"title":"The Island of Floating Stones","level":3,"topic":"sea treasure","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya and Dino sailed east to find a hidden island. The old map showed a coast of floating stones.

At dawn they reached it. Gray stones hung in the air above the beach, bobbing like boats!

"How can stones float?" Dino asked.

Maya read the map again. "It says: the sea breeze keeps them high. Do not speak too loud."

Dino let out a great roar. Boom! Each stone dropped and made the sand shake.

"Oops," he whispered.

A sea eagle swooped down and screeched. Under the fallen stones lay a heap of gold coins and teal beads.

"The treasure!" Maya cheered.

But she did not take it. She left the coins where they lay and only drew a picture in her notebook.

"Real treasure is the trip," she explained.

Dino agreed. Then they sailed home to eat.","cover_scene":"Gray stones floating in the air above a sunny beach on a small island, with a girl and a dinosaur arriving in a wooden sailboat."}

{"title":"The Deep Blue Alphabet Hunt","level":3,"topic":"ocean hunt","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya and Dino dove deep with a list of letters to find.

"A is for anchor," Maya read. An old anchor leaned in the sand, green with weeds.

"B is for beak!" Dino pointed. The octopus has a hard beak hidden under his eight arms.

"C is for coast," said Maya, gazing up at the faint shape of the shore.

"E is for eel." A long eel peeked from a crack and then slid away.

"F is for foam," Dino said, watching bubbles stream toward the light.

"S is for seal!" A gray seal swooped past, chasing a team of fish.

They found a leaf of seaweed, a pearl in a shell, and a rusty wheel.

By the time they reached Z, the sun was low and the sea gleamed like gold.

"Each letter is a treasure," Maya said.","cover_scene":"A girl and a small dinosaur swimming underwater past an old anchor, a seal, and a glowing pearl in an open shell."}

{"title":"Thirty New Creatures Under the Ice","level":3,"topic":"ocean discovery","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Deep beneath the Southern Ocean, scientists found thirty creatures nobody had ever seen.

Maya read the news out loud to Dino. "Look at this one! A sponge that eats animals."

"A sponge?" Dino squeaked. "I thought sponges just sat there!"

Maya nodded. "This one waits on the seafloor and traps tiny beasts that float too near."

She turned the page. "Here are worms that eat bones. When a whale sinks, they clean each bone until it gleams."

Dino leaned closer. "That seems gross."

"It keeps the sea neat," Maya explained.

The last team of photos showed new sea stars, spread out like pale flowers on the cold gray sand.

"How did they reach so deep?" asked Dino.

"A robot boat with a bright beam," said Maya. "It goes where people cannot breathe."

Dino dreamed of the deep all night.","cover_scene":"A glowing deep-sea robot shining its light on pale sea stars and a strange sponge on the dark ocean floor beneath ice."}

{"title":"Dino's Loud Rocket Launch","level":3,"topic":"rocket launch","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya and Dino stood in a field to watch a rocket launch.

"Rockets are louder than thunder," Maya explained. "We need these ear muffs."

Dino pulled a pair over his small green ears.

The speaker counted down. "Three, two, one!"

A bright beam of flame burst out. The ground shook beneath their feet. The sound rolled across the field like a wave hitting a beach.

Dino's teeth chattered. "You were right! That is way louder than thunder!"

The rocket streaked up, leaving a white trail through the clouds. Soon it was a faint speck.

"Where is it going?" Dino asked.

"It carries a robot boat," said Maya. "Someday robots like that will help us reach the deep sea and outer space."

Dino leaned against her. "I dream of reaching space too."

"Then eat your greens," Maya teased.","cover_scene":"A rocket blasting off with a huge flame trail while a girl and a small dinosaur wearing ear muffs watch from a grassy field."}

{"title":"Countdown Club","level":3,"topic":"space launch","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya started a Countdown Club. Every launch day, her friends squeezed into the reading nook to watch live rockets on a screen.

A timer counted down the hours. Dino kept a neat chart of each launch: the date, the team, and where the rocket was headed.

"Today's rocket carries meals and seeds to the space station," Maya read aloud.

"Seeds?" asked Jean.

"Astronauts grow greens up there. Leaves need light, not soil."

The screen showed the rocket leaning on its tower, steaming in the cold dawn air.

"Ten... three... two... one!"

Flames bloomed. The rocket cleared the tower and streaked into a gray cloud.

The club cheered so loud that Maya's mom peeked in.

Dino made a fresh chart for next week.

"Same seats?" he asked.

"Same seats," Maya agreed. "Countdown Club meets again."","cover_scene":"A group of kids and a small dinosaur crowded around a screen showing a rocket lifting off, with a countdown chart on the wall."}

{"title":"Maya Trains to Be an Astronaut","level":2,"topic":"astronaut training","target_skill":"vowel_teams","text":"Maya wants to be an astronaut. So she trains each day.

First she eats a good meal. Oats, green beans, and a peach.

Then she runs down the road. Astronauts need strong legs and feet.

Dino times her. "Fast!" he cheers.

Next, Maya floats in the pool. Space feels a bit like this, she reads. You drift and you do not weigh much at all.

Then she teaches Dino about the moon. "Soon the moon will glow red," she says. "It is called a blood moon."

"Neat!" says Dino.

Maya reads about huge planets that are so light they would float on a sea.

At night she dreams she is in a spaceship. She waves at Earth, a blue and green bead in the dark.

Soon, she thinks. Soon.","cover_scene":"A girl in a homemade cardboard space helmet floating in a swimming pool while a small dinosaur holds a stopwatch at the edge."}

{"title":"Space School for Dino","level":2,"topic":"astronaut school","target_skill":"blends","text":"Dino starts space school. He must train for a whole year!

First, he must swim. Splash! Dino kicks and glides across the pool.

Next, he must climb. He grips the steps and stands on the top plank. He does not slip.

Then comes the spin chair. It spins fast. Dino grins. "More!" he cries.

In class, he studies plants, stars, and space tools. He prints neat notes with a stub of a pen.

He practices first aid. He wraps a cloth on Maya's arm. "Stop the blood flow," he says. "Stay calm."

He learns how the space station spins around Earth. It travels fast, but inside it feels still.

At last, Dino stands tall in a crisp white suit.

"Dino, you pass!" says the teacher.

Maya claps and claps.","cover_scene":"A small dinosaur in a white astronaut training suit climbing a ladder in a big space training center while a girl cheers below."}

transcript.title: The Dino Team by the Sea
transcript.text:
Maya reads about dinosaurs each day. She sees a team of them by the sea.

A big dino eats leaves. He is tall. He can reach the green leaves on a tall tree. Munch, munch!

A small dino eats meat. She is fast. She runs on the sand near the sea.

One dino has a long neck like a boat mast. He goes down to drink. He can float! His neck stays up.

Rain starts to fall. Drip, drip on the leaves. The dinos do not mind the rain. They play in the mud and wait.

Soon the rain goes away. The sun is out. A dino lets out a loud roar. Beat, beat go his big feet on the trail.

Maya reads the last page. Dinosaurs are real, and she can learn more each day. She will read again soon!

chapters.title: The Dinosaur Team
chapters.text:
Sam had a dream about dinosaurs.

In the dream, a green dinosaur ate leaves by the road. Her name was Bean. Bean had a long neck and big feet.

A small dinosaur sat on a boat. His name was Coal. Coal could not reach the leaves.

"Wait!" said Bean. "I can help. We are a team."

Bean bent down. Coal took a big leaf. He ate it and made a happy squeak.

Then they ran on the beach. The sea was blue. The sun was a bright bead in the sky.

Rain fell. Bean and Coal did not mind the rain. They played in the deep, wet sand. They made a road, a moat, and a big dinosaur nest.

Sam woke up.

"Dinosaurs are real!" he said. "They lived long ago. I can read about them today!"

Sam got a dinosaur book. He read each neat page.

What a team!

transcript.title: Dino Eggs in the Oak Tree Trail
transcript.text:
Maya and Jean hike on the oak trail. They seek dinosaur eggs.

"Wait!" says Jean. "I see a nest!"

Three eggs sit on a heap of leaves. Each egg is real. Each egg is the size of a loaf of bread!

A mail truck goes past. The man waves. Maya waves back.

Then they hear a peep. Peep, peep! One egg cracks. A tiny dino peeks out. His neck is neat and long. His feet are teal green!

The baby dino eats a leaf. Then he eats three more leaves. He needs to eat a lot to grow tall.

Maya reads that big dinos once laid eggs like this. Real scientists dig them up today!

The baby dino sleeps by the oak. Maya and Jean tiptoe away. They wave and say, "Sleep well, little dino!"

chapters.title: The Dinosaur on the Boat
chapters.text:
Rex is a big dinosaur. Rex has a dream. He wants to reach the beach.

Rex sees a boat. The boat has one oar. Rex gets in the boat.

"Let's float!" says Rex. The boat starts to float. It goes down the road of green sea.

A seal goes squeak, squeak. "Can I float too?" asks the seal.

"Yes!" says Rex. "Sit here. We can both float."

They float and float. They eat a snack. Rex eats leaves. The seal eats one bean.

Soon they reach the beach! The sand is neat and clean.

Rex sees black coal on the sand. He sees a moat in the sand too.

"Let's dig!" says Rex. They dig a big moat by the sea.

Rex and the seal are a team. A good team!

Did you know? Real kids can read dinosaur facts and play games at National Geographic Kids. Each fact is a treat!

Read on, dinosaur fan!

transcript.title: Ten Dino Eggs Roll Down the Road
transcript.text:
Ten dino eggs roll down the road. Maya sees them all!

The first egg cracks. Out leaps a T. rex. He lets out a great big roar!

The next egg cracks. Out peeks a Stegosaurus. His plates gleam in the sun.

Egg three has a Triceratops. She eats green leaves off a tree. Munch!

Egg four holds a small raptor. He speeds down the road on quick feet.

Egg five is soaked by rain. Out floats a long-neck dino. He reaches way up high.

More eggs crack. Six, seven, eight, nine, ten! Each one is a treat to meet.

The dinos need a home. Maya leads the team to a coast with soft sand and tall trees.

"Stay here," she says. "Eat and sleep and play."

Ten dinos cheer. Maya beams. What a day!

chapters.title: The Dinosaur Beach Feast
chapters.text:
Rex is a big dinosaur. Rex likes the beach.

The beach is warm. The beach is wide. Rex naps on the beach.

Rex can reach a leaf. Rex can reach a seed. Can Rex reach the sea?

Yes! Rex can reach the sea.

A log can float. Rex hops on. The log will float and float. Rex will float to the reef.

A little dino sits on a black rock. It is coal. "My coal is hot," she says. "Coal makes a fire."

Rex sits by the coal. The coal is warm.

Now they eat a feast. A feast of leaves! Each dino gets a treat. Each dino gets a neat green leaf.

"What a feast!" says Rex.

Rex and the little dino are a team. A good team.

They float home on the log. They wave at the beach.

Real kids read about dinosaurs, too. Books and maps tell us each dino name!

transcript.title: The Dino Boat Race
transcript.text:
Maya paints a big boat. Her dino pals want to race on the lake.

T. rex hops in a red boat. Its sail is real cloth. It flaps in the wind.

Stegosaurus takes a green boat. He floats fast! His tail helps him steer.

Triceratops picks a teal boat with a long oar. She rows and rows.

"Ready, set, go!" Maya yells.

The boats speed down the lake. Rain starts to fall. Drip, drip! No one quits.

T. rex leads. Then a gust fills the green sail. Stegosaurus goes past him!

Triceratops keeps her pace. She does not moan. She just rows.

At the last bend, all three boats meet. They reach the coast at the same beat!

"A tie!" Maya cheers. Each dino gets a treat: a heap of sweet green leaves.

What a great day to sail.

chapters.title: The Dinosaur Coal Road
chapters.text:
Rex is a big green dinosaur. Rex likes a treat. Today Rex will reach a real treat.

Rex walks up the coal road. Coal, coal, black coal. The coal is on the road. Rex must not eat coal!

Rex sees a boat. The boat can float. Float, float, little boat. Rex gets on the boat. The boat can float with Rex on it!

The boat rides to a green oak. Under the oak is a feast. A feast! Leaves and beans and plums.

Rex will reach up high. Reach, reach, reach! Rex gets a leaf. What a treat!

"This is a real feast," says Rex. "A real, real treat!"

Rex eats and eats. Then Rex goes back on the boat. Float, float, home.

Real kids can read about real dinosaurs. Nat Geo Kids has facts, games, and art. Each day you can learn a real dinosaur fact. That is a treat too!

chapters.title: Rex Learns the Two-Letter Trick
chapters.text:
Rex met a small dino named Pea.
"Watch this," said Pea. "Two letters can make one sound."
Pea held up met. Then Pea slid an a in.
Met turned into meat!
Rex said it slow. Meat. One sound. E and a say EE.
Pea held up rod. Then Pea slid an a in.
Rod turned into road!
Rex said it slow. Road. One sound. O and a say OH.
Rex tried it all day.
He read team. One sound.
He read each. One sound.
He read leaf. One sound.
He read load. One sound.
He read treat. One sound.
He read real. One sound.
"Real fast!" said Pea.
The team went up the road with a load of leaf snacks.
Each dino got a treat.
At home, Rex read dino facts and games on a kids science page.
"Two letters, one sound," said Rex. "That is the trick!"

chapters.title: Which Shell Will Hatch?
chapters.text:
Shen is a small dinosaur. She sits by a nest. In the nest is one shell.

"Which shell will hatch?" Shen asks. "This one. Watch!"

Shen must watch and wait. She does not wish to miss it. She sits. She watches the shell.

The shell shakes. Chip, chip! A crack! Then a chin pokes out. Then a chubby little chum!

"Hatch! You did hatch!" Shen cheers.

The chick dino wants lunch. Shen must catch a snack. She dashes to a tall branch. She can reach a leaf. What a fine treat!

Munch, munch! The chick did not wish to stop!

Meg watches the chick run. It dashes past the nest.

"Catch it!" Meg yells.

The chick hops back in the shell. It is a good fit.

Meg pats the shell. "Rest, little chick."

transcript.title: Eight Arms Help Out
transcript.text:
Deep in the warm sea, an octopus wakes up. His eight arms stretch out wide.

He has round eyes and no bones at all. He can fit in a small crack in the reef!

Today he wants to help his pals.

A crab is stuck in a coil of rope. The octopus reaches down. One arm loops and pulls. The crab is free!

A baby eel needs a home. The octopus scoops sand and stacks neat stones. Now the eel has a safe cave.

Then a big shark speeds by. The octopus turns pale gray, just like the stones. The shark sails past and sees no one!

At last he floats home to his den. He eats a treat and sleeps.

Eight arms make a great team.

chapters.title: Dash the Dolphin and the Big Catch
chapters.text:
Dash is a dolphin. Dash has a pod.

A pod is a big dolphin family. They swim and play all day.

Dash calls with a whistle. Each dolphin has its own whistle, like a name! Chirp, chirp, chirp!

"Watch me!" says Dash. "Watch me catch a fish!"

Dash makes a click. Click, click! The click bumps a fish and comes back. Now Dash knows where that fish hid!

Splash! What a catch!

"Watch, watch, watch!" chirp the calves. "Catch, catch, catch!"

The calves catch fish too. Munch, munch!

Then Dash sees a shell on the sand. It is pink as a chick's beak.

"Watch this!" says Dash. He tips the shell up on his chin.

The pod chirps and chatters. Such a silly dolphin!

Dash lets the shell drop. Then the pod swims off to catch more fish.

Watch them go! Splash!

transcript.title: Three Hearts in the Shallow Sea
transcript.text:
Maya and Dino splash in the shallow sea. They wish to find the octopus.

"Shh," says Maya. "Look! He is such a champ at hiding."

The octopus shifts his shade. He looks like a shell. Then he looks like a chunk of rock!

Dino chats with him. "Is it true you have three hearts?"

"Yes!" says the octopus. "Thump, thump, thump. Three hearts push my blue blood."

"Wow," whispers Maya.

A shark swims by. The octopus shoots a dash of ink. Whoosh! The shark cannot see. He rushes off.

Then the octopus shows them his shelf of shells. He shares a starfish with Dino.

The sun sinks. Maya must go.

"Thanks for the fun!" she shouts.

Eight arms wave. Three hearts thump. What a chum!

chapters.title: Shy Octopus Has Three Hearts
chapters.text:
Meet Shy. Shy is an octopus. Shy has eight long arms. Shy has three hearts! Thump, thump, thump.

Shy hides in a shell on the sea floor. "Can you find me?" says Shy.

A fish swims by. The fish is pink. "I see you, Shy!"

Shy runs to a rock. Shy can watch the fish from here. "Can you find me?" says Shy.

A crab comes to chat. Chomp, chomp goes the crab.
"I see you, Shy!"

Shy puffs a bit of ink. Poof! Shy is gone. "Can you find me?" says Shy.

The fish looks. The crab looks. No Shy!

Then Shy pops up. "Here I am! Watch me!"

Shy can catch a snack with one long arm. Shy can catch a shell with two.

Thump, thump, thump go the three hearts.

"I like to hide," says Shy. "But I like pals best."

transcript.title: Dino's Deep Sea Ship
transcript.text:
Dino builds a ship. It is thick and strong.

"Let's check the deep sea!" he shouts.

Maya hops in. The ship chugs out past the wharf.

Splash! Down they go. Fish flash by the glass.

"Which way?" asks Dino.

"That way," says Maya. "To the shipwreck!"

The shipwreck rests in the sand. Shells cling to it. A crab pinches at a chain.

Then a shape shifts in the shade. It is the octopus!

He has no shell and no bones. He can slip in a thin crack much smaller than his head.

"Wow!" whispers Dino.

The octopus shows them a chest. Inside are shiny dishes and a gold chunk.

"We should leave it," says Maya. "This is his shop, not ours."

The octopus waves. The ship rushes up. What a champ of a trip!

chapters.title: Blink the Octopus Packs a Snack
chapters.text:
Blink is a small octopus. She has eight long arms and big round eyes.

Blink lives where the sea is warm. Most octopuses stay down on the sand. Blink stays there too.

"Here I go!" says Blink. "I will grab a snack from the sand!"

She slips past a crab. She spins past a clam. She stops by a flat gray rock.

"Here I go!" says Blink. "I will grab a snack from this rock!"

Snap! A crab grabs it first. The crab swims off fast.

"Here I go!" says Blink. "I will grab a snack from that shell!"

Blink slides her arm in the shell. Plop! A small clam drops out.

Blink grins. She spins. Her eight arms flip and flap.

"Here is my snack!" says Blink. "It came from the sand, and it is the best snack of all!"

transcript.title: The Island of Floating Stones
transcript.text:
Maya and Dino sailed east to find a hidden island. The old map showed a coast of floating stones.

At dawn they reached it. Gray stones hung in the air above the beach, bobbing like boats!

"How can stones float?" Dino asked.

Maya read the map again. "It says: the sea breeze keeps them high. Do not speak too loud."

Dino let out a great roar. Boom! Each stone dropped and made the sand shake.

"Oops," he whispered.

A sea eagle swooped down and screeched. Under the fallen stones lay a heap of gold coins and teal beads.

"The treasure!" Maya cheered.

But she did not take it. She left the coins where they lay and only drew a picture in her notebook.

"Real treasure is the trip," she explained.

Dino agreed. Then they sailed home to eat.

chapters.title: Crab Kid and the Tide Pool Crew
chapters.text:
Crab Kid slips into the tide pool.

The sun is bright. The water is cool.

A small snail slides up a rock. "Slow down!" says Crab Kid.

A green crab claps his claws. Snap, snap!

A star fish sticks to a stone. It will not let go.

Crab Kid spots a clam in the sand. The clam is shut tight.

"Can you help?" asks Crab Kid.

The snail slides. The star fish sticks. The green crab grabs.

Plop! The clam flips free.

Just then, a gray arm slips out of a crack. An octopus!

The crew does not flap or run.

Octopuses have eight long arms and big round eyes. They live in seas all over the world. Most stay down on the sand.

This one waves one arm. Hi!

Crab Kid waves back. "Come play in our pool."

The sun sets. The tide pool is a snug home for all.

Maya and Dino dove deep with a list of letters to find.

"B is for beak!" Dino pointed. The octopus has a hard beak hidden under his eight arms.

By the time they reached Z, the sun was low and the sea gleamed like gold.

"Each letter is a treasure," Maya said.

chapters.title: Green Dino and the Gray Truck
chapters.text:
Green Dino wakes at day break. He sees a big gray truck on the street. The truck has a steep ramp and three green flags.

"Can I play?" asks Green Dino.

The truck man claps. "Free ride today!"

Green Dino steps up the ramp. His feet stomp. The truck starts with a snap and a squeak.

They drive past tall trees. They drive past a stream. A bee sails by. Green Dino stays still and keeps his tail in.

They stop by a clay hill. Green Dino sees deep tracks in the clay. Big tracks! Three toes!

"Those tracks may be from a dino long ago," says the truck man. "They stay in stone for a long, long time."

Green Dino grins. He steps in the tracks. His feet fit!

The gray truck drives home. Green Dino sleeps and dreams of free days, green trees, and play.

transcript.text:
Deep beneath the Southern Ocean, scientists found thirty creatures nobody had ever seen.

"How did they reach so deep?" asked Dino.

"A robot boat with a bright beam," said Maya. "It goes where people cannot breathe."

Dino dreamed of the deep all night.

chapters.title: Stella and the Space Truck
chapters.text:
Stella drives a big space truck. The truck is gray and green.

She stops at the moon. Thump! Stomp! Her boots make tracks in the dust.

Stella grins. She grabs her camera. Snap! She takes a crisp photo of the stars.

On Earth, kids send in photos too. Real scientists snap pictures of their work. More than 220 people sent in the best ones! Stella wants to send hers.

A small rock slides past. Stella claps. "Stop, rock!" she calls. The rock spins and drops.

She climbs back in the truck. The trip home is long. Stella sleeps in her seat.

Drip, drop, the rain taps as she lands. Her dad stands by the gate.

"Did you get a good snap?" he asks.

Stella grins big. "I got the stars, the dust, and my own tracks!"

Her photo sits on the wall now. A space truck. A moon. Tracks in the dust.

transcript.title: Dino's Loud Rocket Launch
transcript.text:
Maya and Dino stood in a field to watch a rocket launch.

"Rockets are louder than thunder," Maya explained. "We need these ear muffs."

Dino pulled a pair over his small green ears.

The speaker counted down. "Three, two, one!"

A bright beam of flame burst out. The ground shook beneath their feet. The sound rolled across the field like a wave hitting a beach.

Dino's teeth chattered. "You were right! That is way louder than thunder!"

The rocket streaked up, leaving a white trail through the clouds. Soon it was a faint speck.

"Where is it going?" Dino asked.

"It carries a robot boat," said Maya. "Someday robots like that will help us reach the deep sea and outer space."

Dino leaned against her. "I dream of reaching space too."

"Then eat your greens," Maya teased.

chapters.title: The Night Gate Rocket
chapters.text:
Maya stands at the tall gate by the launch pad. Past the gate, a white rocket waits in the wide open space.

"Nine... five... one!" the crew calls.

Flames blaze. The rocket makes a huge sound, like thunder that will not quit. Maya claps her hands over her ears and grins.

Up it climbs, past the pines, past the clouds. Soon it is just a bright spark that seems to shine like a late star.

Inside, the crew floats. They wave at a small camera. Maya waves back, even though home is far below them.

"Can I make one?" she asks.

Her dad smiles. "NASA has a plan for kids. You can build a bubble-powered rocket with tape and a plastic tube. No flames, just fizz."

So Maya races home. She tapes her rocket, shakes the fizz, and steps back.

POP! It flies up the drive, and Maya cheers like a whole launch crew.

transcript.title: Countdown Club
transcript.text:
Maya started a Countdown Club. Every launch day, her friends squeezed into the reading nook to watch live rockets on a screen.

A timer counted down the hours. Dino kept a neat chart of each launch: the date, the team, and where the rocket was headed.

"Today's rocket carries meals and seeds to the space station," Maya read aloud.

"Seeds?" asked Jean.

"Astronauts grow greens up there. Leaves need light, not soil."

The screen showed the rocket leaning on its tower, steaming in the cold dawn air.

"Ten... three... two... one!"

Flames bloomed. The rocket cleared the tower and streaked into a gray cloud.

The club cheered so loud that Maya's mom peeked in.

Dino made a fresh chart for next week.

"Same seats?" he asked.

"Same seats," Maya agreed. "Countdown Club meets again."

chapters.title: Jake and the Bubble Rocket
chapters.text:
Jake made a rocket at home from a tube, some tape, and a paper cone. NASA kids make these too, and they call it a bubble rocket.

"This one will shine," Jake said. He made a huge white stripe down the side. Then he wrote his name on the nose.

Jake took the rocket past the gate and set it on the flat stone. He shook the tube. Inside, bubbles began to slide and spin.

"Five, four, three, two, one!"

POP! The rocket rose like a spark. It flew above the pine tree, above the kite, above the line of clouds. Jake smiled a wide smile.

The rocket came down in the tall grass. Jake ran to take it home.

"Same time tomorrow?" Mom asked.

"Yes," Jake said. "Next time I will make it go twice as high."

transcript.title: Maya Trains to Be an Astronaut
transcript.text:
Maya wants to be an astronaut. So she trains each day.

First she eats a good meal. Oats, green beans, and a peach.

Then she runs down the road. Astronauts need strong legs and feet.

Dino times her. "Fast!" he cheers.

Next, Maya floats in the pool. Space feels a bit like this, she reads. You drift and you do not weigh much at all.

Then she teaches Dino about the moon. "Soon the moon will glow red," she says. "It is called a blood moon."

"Neat!" says Dino.

Maya reads about huge planets that are so light they would float on a sea.

At night she dreams she is in a spaceship. She waves at Earth, a blue and green bead in the dark.

Soon, she thinks. Soon.

chapters.title: Nicole Mann and the Floating Lime
chapters.text:
Nicole Mann is a real astronaut. She is the first Native American woman to fly to space. She left home in October and made her way to the space station, high above us.

On the station, nothing stays still. A lime can float past your nose! Nicole grabs it and takes a bite. Juice does not drip here. It makes a tiny globe that shines like glass.

Breakfast comes in a tube. Soup comes in a tube too. There is no time for a mess, so every plate and spoon has tape or a clip.

Nicole looks out the wide window. She can see a huge blue Earth spin below. In five more minutes, the sun will rise again. Up here, it rises sixteen times a day!

She waves at the white clouds over her home state.

"Same planet," she smiles. "Just a different place to stand."

transcript.title: Space School for Dino
transcript.text:
Dino starts space school. He must train for a whole year!

First, he must swim. Splash! Dino kicks and glides across the pool.

Next, he must climb. He grips the steps and stands on the top plank. He does not slip.

Then comes the spin chair. It spins fast. Dino grins. "More!" he cries.

In class, he studies plants, stars, and space tools. He prints neat notes with a stub of a pen.

He practices first aid. He wraps a cloth on Maya's arm. "Stop the blood flow," he says. "Stay calm."

He learns how the space station spins around Earth. It travels fast, but inside it feels still.

At last, Dino stands tall in a crisp white suit.

"Dino, you pass!" says the teacher.

Maya claps and claps.

chapters.title: Five Space Tubes
chapters.text:
Sam made a home in space. It had five long tubes. Each tube had a wide window.

Sam woke at nine. He ate a bite of cake from a bag. Then he went to the globe room.

Out the glass, he saw the big blue globe. That is home. Sam waved at home.

A new space telescope will rise soon. It will take a close look at stars. Sam had to help it.

He took some tape. He taped a loose pipe in the last tube. The fix was done in five clicks.

"Nice!" said Kim. "That tape saved the day."

Then the moon came in sight. It made a red glow, like a rose. Kim and Sam just gazed.

"Can we stay up late?" said Sam.

"Yes," said Kim. "The moon will not hide. This is a fine time."

The five tubes spun in the black sky, and the red moon shone.

transcript.title: The Cotton Candy Planet
transcript.text:
Maya and Dino fly a small spaceship past the stars.

"Stop!" says Dino. "What is that pink blob?"

It is a super-puff planet. It is huge, but it is not solid. It is less dense than cotton candy!

"Can we land?" asks Dino.

"No," says Maya. "We would sink right through the fluff."

They drift close. The planet glows pink and blue. Wisps of gas swirl and drift like smoke.

Dino sticks his snout out. "It smells like nothing," he grins.

"That is a lunar eclipse," Maya says. "Scientists study it with a strong space telescope."

chapters.title: The Moon Turns Red

Sam and Jane sit on the lawn.
The sun is gone. Here comes the moon.
"It came up late," says Jane.

Sam made a plan. He got his tape and a tube.
He made a small scope with the tube.
Jane came close. She gave the tube a look.
"I can see the red moon!" she says.
They take the tube in the game with them.
Sam gave Jane a slice of cake.
They ate the cake and sat up late.
The red moon shone on Jane and Sam.
Then they came home.
"Same time next time?" says Sam.
"Yes!" says Jane. "Same moon. Same cake."

transcript.text:
Scientists built a giant space telescope called Roman. It will travel past the clouds and stare deep into the stars.

Maya and Dino watched the news clip. The telescope stood in a clean white room while workers in crisp suits checked every screw.

"What will it find?" Dino asked.

"Can it spot my street?" Dino grinned.

"It stares the other way," Maya laughed. "Straight out past the Milky Way."

They drew their own telescope plans on a big sheet. Dino sketched a stand with strong legs. Maya printed a list of stars to study.

That night they climbed onto the back steps with binoculars.

"I see a smudge!" Dino whispered.

"That smudge," said Maya, "is a whole galaxy."

chapters.title: The Soft Puff Planet
chapters.text:
Sam had a dream at night.

He went up past the moon.

He saw a big planet way out in space.

"Wait," said Sam. "Is it real?"

It was pink. It was soft. It was light as cotton candy!

Sam did not need a rope. He did not need a crane.

He just gave it a poke.

Poof! His hand sank in deep.

The soft planet did not break. It did not rain on him. It just went boing.

Sam made a seat in the fluff. He sat back and took a nap.

The moon shone. The stars shone too.

Then Sam woke up at home in his bed.

"That was a neat dream," he said.

He told his mom, "Some planets are real puffs! They float. They are light."

Mom said, "Then take me next time."

Sam said, "Wait for me at nine. We can go to the moon."

transcript.title: Grandpa and the Museum Bones
transcript.text:
Grandpa took Maya to the dinosaur museum on a bright Saturday.

The first skeleton stood in the front hall. Its spine stretched from the steps to the stairs. Maya's mouth dropped open.

"Stegosaurus," Grandpa read from the small plaque. "Those plates on its back might have helped it stay cool."

They strolled past a Triceratops skull with three strong horns. They stopped at a glass case of speckled eggs, still cracked from the day they hatched.

In the lab, a scientist brushed grit from a clawed foot. She let Maya hold a stone tooth. It was heavy and smooth.

"How do you know where to dig?" Maya asked.

"We study the ground," the scientist smiled. "Then we hope."

On the drive home, Maya sketched every skeleton she could remember.

"Next trip," said Grandpa, "you can be my guide."

chapters.title: The Real Dinosaur Team
chapters.text:
Maya and Grandpa went to the dinosaur museum. A real T. rex stood in the big hall. Its teeth were as long as Maya's hand.

"Did it eat meat?" Maya asked.

"It ate a lot of meat," Grandpa said. "But it did not eat kids who read books."

Maya laughed. She could not reach the tail, but she could see each bone.

A guide came by with a tray. "Our team digs up bones," she said. "Sometimes a bone has a break in it. We clean each piece and put it back."

Maya took a seat and drew the great beast. She made the head big and the feet neat.

At the end, they took a break for a snack. Grandpa said, "At home you can play dinosaur games on the museum website. You can even match real fossil photos."

Maya beamed. "One day I will dig up a real one," she said. "That is my dream."

transcript.title: Maya the Museum Guide
transcript.text:
Maya kept her promise. On the next trip, she was the guide.

"Step this way," she told Grandpa, sweeping her arm toward the fossil hall.

She stopped at a slab of gray stone. "These are tracks. A dinosaur strolled through mud, and the mud turned to stone."

Grandpa crouched down. "It was in a hurry. The strides are long."

"Exactly!" Maya beamed.

At a screen, they played a fossil game. Maya dragged scattered bones into place until a skeleton stood complete.

"Which dinosaur?" the screen asked.

Maya studied the spiky plates and the small skull. "Stegosaurus," she typed. A star flashed. Correct!

Then she sketched a Triceratops, starting with its stout frame and finishing with three sharp horns.

Grandpa clapped. "You explain things better than the signs do."

Maya grinned. "That is because I want to be a paleontologist."

chapters.title: Maya's Dinosaur Tail Dig

Maya had a dream. In her dream, she found a real dinosaur tail.

In 2026, a museum in New York City let kids dig for real fossils. Maya could not wait. "This is a dream day!" she said.

Her team took small picks and brushes. Maya read the sign. The sign said: Dig with care. Do not break the bones.

Maya read it again. Then her team began.

Brush, brush, brush. Maya saw a great gray shape in the sand. It was long. It was real!

"A tail!" she said. "A real dinosaur tail!"

Her team came to see. The tail was great and long, like a great gray rope.

A guide said, "That tail helped the dinosaur turn fast. Do not break it. Brush slow."

Maya did not break one bit. She took a break, had a snack, and read more signs.

Her team cheered. Her dream was real.

transcript.title: The Backyard Fossil Hunt
transcript.text:
Saturday morning, Maya grabbed a small brush, a spoon, and a plastic crate.

"Fossil hunt!" she announced. Dino stomped after her into the creek bed behind the house.

Grandpa explained the rules. "Look at the flat stones first. Split them gently. Never climb the steep bank."

Maya scanned the gravel. She spotted a stone with a swirl pressed into it, like a tiny snail curled in sleep.

"An ammonite!" Grandpa said. "It swam in a sea that covered this land long ago."

Dino found a stone with thin stripes, but Grandpa smiled. "That one is just a pretty rock."

"Rocks are still great," Dino sniffed, and dropped it in the crate anyway.

By noon they had three shells, one leaf print, and muddy knees.

Maya labeled each find with a strip of tape.

"Museum," she declared, "in my bedroom."

chapters.title: Maya and the Great Beach Bone
chapters.text:
Maya had a dream. In the dream, she found a real dinosaur on the beach. Was the dream real? She had to go and see.

At dawn she took a pail, a brush, and a book to read. The sea was gray. The waves would break on the sand, then break again.

Maya dug. She hit something hard. "Don't break it!" she said. She read the tag on her kit: GO SLOW. So she went slow.

A bone! Then a long, curved tail. A real tail, with real ridges. Her team came running. "This is a great find!" said Dean.

Maya read the shape of the tail like a map. Her dream was real.

The team sent a photo to the big museum in New York, where kids read about dinosaurs every day. "A real tail," wrote the museum. "Great work, team!"

Maya's dream did not break. It came true.

transcript.title: Maya's Bedroom Museum
transcript.text:
Maya spread her fossils across the shelf under her window.

First came the ammonite, curled like a sleeping snail. Then three speckled shells, the leaf print, and the pretty striped rock that Dino refused to leave behind.

She printed a label for each one and propped them against the glass.

"Grand opening at three," she announced.

Dino swept the floor with his tail. Grandpa brought crackers and a stack of plates.

At three o'clock, Mom, Dad, and Jean crowded into the small bedroom.

Maya stood straight and began. "This ammonite swam in a shallow sea before any person walked on Earth."

Jean asked a question. Maya answered it perfectly.

"How much is a ticket?" Dad teased.

"Free," said Maya. "But scientists always need helpers. Next Saturday, bring a brush."

Everyone promised they would.

chapters.title: Maya's Museum Dream Day
chapters.text:
Maya had a dream about a museum full of bones. In her dream, she could read every sign. The next day, her dad said, "Let's make that dream real."

At the American Museum of Natural History, kids can learn real dinosaur facts. Maya wanted to read them all.

A guide named Jean met her team at the door. "Our team digs, cleans, and guards these bones," she said. "One slip can break a bone that waited millions of years."

Maya held her breath. She did not want to break anything, not even a leaf.

She stopped at a great long tail. The tail curved above her head like a bridge. "Is this tail real?" she asked.

"Every piece is real," Jean said. "Read the sign."

Maya did read it, slow and clear. A great grin spread over her face.

"My dream came true," she said. "Our team should come back next week."

transcript.title: Draw a Dinosaur
transcript.text:
On the museum website, Maya found a drawing lesson.

"Start with the skeleton," the screen explained. "Bones first, skin last."

Maya sketched a long spine that curved like a stretched spring. She added a small skull, a strong pair of back legs, and a stiff tail for balance.

"It looks like a bird," Dino said, peering over her shoulder.

"Because it is one, sort of," Maya said. "Scientists think birds came from dinosaurs like this."

Next she drew muscles over the bones, then a skin of small scales.

"What color?" Dino asked.

Maya stopped her pencil. "Nobody knows for certain. So I can choose."

She picked bright stripes of green and blue, with a splash of red across the snout.

Dino studied the finished drawing for a long moment.

"That," he said proudly, "looks exactly like my grandfather."

chapters.title: Maya and the Curved Claw Puzzle
chapters.text:
At the museum, Maya leaned close to a glass case. Inside sat a curved claw, gray as rain and longer than her hand.

"Can you guess which dinosaur wore this?" asked Dr. Reyes, a real paleontologist.

Maya read the sign slowly. The claw came from a beast that once chased meals across a steamy plain. Its feet left deep trails in the mud, and the mud turned to stone.

"How do you learn so much from one piece?" Maya asked.

Dr. Reyes explained that scientists compare each bone to bones we see today. Little clues team up until a whole creature appears.

Then she showed Maya a website for kids. On it, Maya could match fossil photos, rebuild a skeleton, and draw what a dinosaur may have looked like.

Maya painted a tail, a beak, and eight sharp claws.

"Natural science is mostly good questions," said Dr. Reyes.

Maya grinned. She had plenty.

transcript.title: The Dinosaur Art Contest
transcript.text:
The library announced a dinosaur art contest. First prize was a box of pastels.

Maya practiced every evening. She drew a Spinosaurus with a tall sail, a Brachiosaurus stretching toward treetops, and a sprinting raptor with sharp claws.

"Which one should I enter?" she asked Dino.

Dino studied each sketch slowly. "The raptor. It looks like it might spring off the page."

On Friday, Maya pinned her drawing to the display board. Sixteen other pictures hung beside it: glittery stegosaurs, a purple T. rex, even a dinosaur wearing striped socks.

The judge strolled past, stopping at each one.

Maya's stomach flipped.

"Second place," the judge finally said, pressing a blue ribbon into Maya's hand. "Wonderful sense of movement."

First place went to the dinosaur in striped socks.

Maya laughed. "Honestly? Those socks were brilliant."

chapters.title: Maya and the Stone Egg Nest
chapters.text:
Maya wore her tan hat to the dig site. The whole team came early, before the sun got hot.

"Today we hunt for a nest," said Dr. Pine. "Dinosaur eggs turn to stone over time."

Maya took a fine brush and swept the dust. Something smooth came into view. It was a pale stone shape, round as a plum.

"An egg!" Maya spoke in a whisper, like the whole desert might wake.

Dr. Pine came close. She let Maya compare the stone egg to a hen egg from her lunch pail. The dinosaur egg was three times as wide!

Near the egg lay one thin bone, no longer than Maya's hand. A baby bone.

Back home, Maya read the dinosaur news online. Kids all over the globe hunt for bones and eggs, just like she did.

Maya wrote in her note pad: "I found a whole nest. I hope the babies made it home."

transcript.title: Socks the Dinosaur
transcript.text:
The striped socks gave Maya an idea.

She drew a brand new dinosaur and named him Socks. He had a stout body, a spiky crest, and four bright socks that never slipped off.

In her sketchbook, Socks did splendid things. He slid down snowy slopes. He stomped through swamps without getting his feet damp. He served snacks at a dinosaur school.

Dino read every page twice. "You should send these somewhere."

So Maya scanned her drawings and submitted them to a website where students share artwork.

Weeks passed. She almost stopped checking.

Then an email arrived: Socks the Dinosaur was selected for the spring showcase.

Maya sprinted through the house, waving the printed page.

Grandpa framed it for the bedroom museum, right beside the ammonite.

"Two exhibits now," he said. "Ancient bones and brand new art."

chapters.title: Maya and the Egg That Came Home
chapters.text:
Maya came to the lab with a stone egg in a box. The egg was made of hard grey rock, and it felt like a smooth bone.

"Time to look close," said Dr. Rose. She made a note on her pad.

Maya came near. She spoke in a quiet voice. "Can we compare it?"

On the screen was a museum site for kids called OLogy. It had games where you compare fossil photos and name each one. Maya spoke the names out loud. She spoke them again.

The egg was round like a small globe. Dr. Rose held up a bone, then the stone egg, then the whole picture. "Compare the shape," she said. "The whole nest was made of eggs like this."

Maya came home with the box. She spoke to her mom about the globe-shaped egg, the bone, the whole nest, and the time she made a real note like a scientist.
